text: The post charge-off recovery is event-driven and has no REST operation of its own; the module's two published operations belong to RWB-S7-E6013-APP (API-S7-001, right C) and RWB-S7-E6018-APP (API-S7-002, right A).
why: No source publishes a recovery operation and the legacy Endpoints table repeats the scan and the committee decision for every S7 story.
read: TSD S7 T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD S7 A2.15.4; legacy RWB-E6-027 Endpoints

text: The step consumes the payment received after charge-off event of rwb-payment on rwb.payment.events.v1, with the naming rule shape rwb.payment.<Event>.v1 and its retry and .dlt topics; the Event token and the payload are placeholders; the consumer group and the inbox row are this service's and no outbox row is written.
why: The connection matrix gives S7 'T E' into P8, the naming rule fixes the topic shape, and TSD S7 T5.3 publishes no consumed event.
read: Context pack connection matrix row S7 and naming rules; Template and Rules v1 R4; TSD S7 T5.3

text: The payment, account and customer facts are read on rwb-source-data's contract under /api/recovery/source-data/v1 (DP-05), and rwb-writeoff holds no v_ace_* grant and copies no ACE row.
why: Architecture v5 lets only rwb-source-data read the 30 v_ace_* views, and DP-05 gives the read through the owner's contract or the service's own views.
read: Context pack naming rules and ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 8

text: The agency fee schedule and the placement facts are reference data read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case under the default ruling, at their version, and never as a partner table.
why: The default ruling places parameters and reference data with P3 rwb-case, and no source this story may read names an owner for the fee schedule.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-07; context pack; TSD S7 T3.1

text: R-WO-37's agency fee is split: rwb-partner owns the fee calculation (FEAT-PRM-07) and the placement (FEAT-PRM-06), while rwb-writeoff posts the recovery as income and records the fee reference returned for the placement.
why: The rule action and the S9 feature claim the same calculation and no source says which service owns the amount or the posting.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-WO-37; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 rows FEAT-PRM-06 and FEAT-PRM-07

text: The WO package is a governed copy delivered to rwb-writeoff by rwb-decision (DP-04), so the rule version in force is read from the local package and not on a REST call; the local decision record is the DP-03 record and the central ledger entry is P7's.
why: The Temporal and Drools Design says rule models are governed once in rwb-decision and copied to each owner, the matrix gives S7 only Temporal to P7, and DP-04 is not in the plan's pattern set.
read: Context pack Temporal and Drools slide 12 and connection matrix row S7; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04

text: The income posting to ALS and the general ledger is raised as the postProceeds activity on rwb-payment's queue, and the posted date it confirms is written to write_off.posted_date (DF-FIN-016).
why: Temporal and Drools slide 12 names Payment.postProceeds in the L4 activity contracts, the matrix gives S7 Temporal to P8, and TSD S7 T5.1 publishes no external interface and T5.2 no integration module.
read: Context pack Temporal and Drools slide 12 and connection matrix row S7; TSD S7 T5.1 and T5.2; FSD S7 A2.15.2

text: PLACED_WITH_AGENCY, CASE_CLOSED and PAYMENT_MATCHED are the WRITEOFF states of write_off.state, and the legacy line 'the case moves to PAYMENT_MATCHED' is the stage move answered to rwb-case and applied by the parent CaseWorkflow.
why: The rules table gives the from and to states of R-WO-37 and R-WO-49, TSD S7 T4 gives the WRITEOFF machine, and no source publishes a case-move operation.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-37 and R-WO-49; TSD S7 T4; context pack workflow row and slide 13

text: The step publishes no event; WriteOffApproved (EV-24) stays the approval path's on rwb.writeoff.events.v1, and the missing recovery event is carried as a reporting gap with one proposed event on the same topic rather than a name invented here.
why: TSD S7 T5.3 publishes one event for the module, rwb-reporting listens to S7 events, and no source gives the recovery an event name or a payload.
read: TSD S7 T5.3; context pack ownership row 'Events (1) EV-24' and connection matrix row P9; Template and Rules v1 R4

text: The release 30 April 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative, and wave 4 is confirmed because EP06 maps to wave 4 and rwb-writeoff is created in wave 4.
why: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 gives EP06 wave 4, the context pack gives rwb-writeoff wave 4, and the dates are unchanged and tentative.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and U7; context pack service row; legacy RWB-E6-027 Epic row

text: The agency fee is carried as a property of the decision record only: write_off has no fee column in TSD S7 T3.1 and the fee reference is not a business value of this service.
why: R-WO-37 asks for the fee and the physical schema gives no field for it; adding a column would change the DB story of the service.
read: TSD S7 T3.1 (DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020) and T3.2; FSD S7 A2.15.3.1
